title: Collection: Corralling Your Stuff
coreMove: Sweep every loose piece of stuff into visible capture points before deciding what any of it means.
sourcePressure: Collection is a full sweep of physical and mental incompletes, not selective note-taking, so loose material stops distracting attention from outside the system.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Capturing only important-looking tasks and leaving small scraps, objects, and mental loops outside the system.
sourceAnchorNote: The source sidecar contains no chapter-specific named people, named studies, or named places. Use only the listed GTD terms, official metadata, or supported artifacts; do not invent anecdotes.

sourceAnchors.name: Corralling Your Stuff
sourceAnchors.detail: The locked chapter title and sidecar frame collection as gathering stuff and incompletes into capture.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Stuff is whatever has a hook in your attention, even if it looks too small to deserve a task name yet.

sourceAnchors.name: full sweep of physical and mental incompletes
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar identifies a comprehensive sweep as the chapter pressure.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The sweep works because nothing gets to stay half-trusted in a pocket, on a counter, or in your head.

hook: stress is not about having too much to do
a messy desk proves the system is broken
counterintuition: the real problem is not time but attention
this is not about doing more but doing what matters
the simple move is actually the powerful one
tryThisNow: set a timer and write everything down
pick one task and make it specific
review your list and choose a priority
examples: timestamp plus name plus laptop plus decision repeated across all six examples
home kitchen clutter as mental-load shorthand

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: a veterinary reception desk after a vaccine clinic
exampleSpecs.audience: a receptionist holding callbacks, forms, and owner questions
exampleSpecs.stakes: a lab result or medication refill could vanish under check-in traffic
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The waiting room is finally quiet when Megan empties coat pockets, sticky flags, and phone scraps into one intake tray without sorting.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a leash hook swaying by the reception counter

exampleSpecs.domain: a commercial fishing boat captain after a harbor inspection
exampleSpecs.audience: a captain with repairs, permits, and crew messages spread across the boat
exampleSpecs.stakes: one uncollected permit note could keep the boat tied up
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Diesel hangs in the wheelhouse as Jack walks stern to bow with a clipboard, gathering every loose repair and permit reminder.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a damp clipboard on the wheelhouse console

exampleSpecs.domain: a bridal alterations shop after a Saturday fitting rush
exampleSpecs.audience: a shop owner surrounded by pins, receipts, and client promises
exampleSpecs.stakes: one hem change could be remembered only after the bride returns
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Do not fix it yet," Etienne tells his assistant, placing every slip and fabric tag into the collection box first.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: silver pins scattered beside a fabric tag

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional library system sorting branch requests after a bookmobile route
exampleSpecs.audience: a librarian collecting rural branch needs from many channels
exampleSpecs.stakes: a missing audiobook hold or printer issue could become next week’s complaint
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Ingrid one angry patron call to see that the problem was not the branch request itself; it had never entered collection.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a bookmobile route sheet folded in quarters

exampleSpecs.domain: a robotics repair bench after a school competition weekend
exampleSpecs.audience: a mentor with spare parts, student requests, and broken components everywhere
exampleSpecs.stakes: a motor replacement could be lost before the next build session
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Which pile gets judged first if Akira has not yet gathered the stripped gear, the parent email, and the drivetrain note into one capture path?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stripped gear beside a battery tester

exampleSpecs.domain: a boutique hotel front desk during a shift change
exampleSpecs.audience: a front-desk lead collecting guest promises before handoff
exampleSpecs.stakes: a late checkout or allergy request could remain only in a tired clerk’s memory
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You can feel the handoff change when Sofia writes every loose guest promise onto the shift capture sheet before discussing any solution.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a brass room key tag beside the shift sheet

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: recognize hidden incompletes in physical objects

tryThisNowSpec: Do a two-minute sweep of one small area and capture every object or thought that represents an unfinished commitment.
